      <title>Men deported from US bound and beaten in Equatorial Guinea detention hotel, lawyers say</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/sep/18/us-men-deported-hotel-equatorial-guinea</link>
      <description><p>Group trapped at Hotel Bamy after US removal as rights groups sound alarm over poor conditions and violence</p><p></p><p>Two men that the Trump administration expelled to Equatorial Guinea were bound, fitted with bags over their heads, beaten and pushed down a flight of stairs, all in plain view of other US deportees, according to witnesses and human rights lawyers.</p><p>The men – one from Egypt and one from Eritrea – were then taken to a prison. About 30 detainees from the US remain trapped at a hotel in the outskirts of the coastal city of Malabo after being deported from the US. Detainees have said they believe the men were beaten for telling the press and human rights advocates about the poor conditions and violence inside the hotel, and that they are haunted by flashbacks and terrified they will be retaliated against next.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/sep/18/us-men-deported-hotel-equatorial-guinea">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/18/survivor-panic-struggle-breathe-nigeria-prison-cell-died-minna</link>
      <description><p>Police fire teargas as protests break out in city of Minna after deaths of suspected illegal goldminers, many of whom were children</p><p>Survivors from a prison cell in Nigeria where 37 suspected illegal goldminers died while in the custody of a paramilitary group this week have recounted their panic and struggle for breath, as police on Friday fired teargas at people protesting against the deaths and imposed an overnight curfew in the city of Minna.</p><p>The victims – many of whom were children – were found dead on Thursday in the cells of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), which had raided suspected illegal goldmines and ⁠locked up dozens of miners in the city, the state capital of the mineral-rich state of Niger.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/18/survivor-panic-struggle-breathe-nigeria-prison-cell-died-minna">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>New cat species identified for first time in more than a century in Bolivia</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/17/new-cat-species-identified-bolivia</link>
      <description><p>New species of wild feline was discovered in Bolivia’s Yungas forest that is smaller than the average domestic ⁠cat</p><p>A diminutive wild cat that inhabits Bolivia’s ⁠cloud forest has been identified as a previously unknown species, marking the first time a new living feline species has been formally named and described in more than a century.</p><p>The cat, called tilcayo by local communities, is part of a group called tiger ⁠cats found across much of South ⁠America. It was found in Bolivia’s ​lush Yungas forest, a mountainous region where forests are often covered by clouds and surrounded by high humidity, according to researchers. It measures about 18in (46cm) long and weighs about 3lb (1.4kg), making it smaller than the average domestic ⁠cat.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/17/new-cat-species-identified-bolivia">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Passionate documentary maker  won international acclaim for unsparing but poetic films exploring the impact of the Pinochet regime in Chile </p><p>Patricio Guzmán, the film-maker who chronicled Chile’s bloody 1970s political strife and its subsequent social and political turmoil in films such as The Battle of Chile and Nostalgia for the Light, has died aged 85. <a href="https://www.emol.com/noticias/Espectaculos/2026/09/15/1211542/muere-cineasta-patricio-guzman.html">According to Chilean news outlet Emol</a>, Guzmán died on Tuesday in Paris after a cardiorespiratory arrest.</p><p>Guzmán’s chief preoccupation throughout his career was the carnage unleashed by Augusto Pinochet’s coup in 1973 against Salvador Allende, Chile’s elected president. <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/film/2012/jul/20/patricio-guzman-chile-master-documentary">He later told the Guardian</a>: “I’m a film-maker who was very marked by the ways of the dictator. It has remained with me for ever. I cannot leave it behind.” However, he resisted the idea that he was an activist, political film-maker, adding: “I’m not a sociologist. Neither am I a politician. I make films that are metaphorical and poetic; I interpret reality through my own personal way of looking.”</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/sep/16/battle-of-chile-director-patricio-guzman-dies-aged-85">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Trump’s battle to rename the Kennedy Center has put its future at risk</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/sep/19/trump-kennedy-center-future</link>
      <description><p>The president has threatened to block renovations and suggested the landmark could be demolished after courts ruled against his bid to rename it  </p><p>It was born with the world premiere of Leonard Bernstein’s Mass. “Young people will come here and they will see this cultural centre,” Rose Kennedy, the mother of slain US president John F Kennedy, <a href="https://wtop.com/dc/2026/09/from-george-washington-to-jfk-a-history-of-the-kennedy-center/">said at that opening night gala</a>. “They will carry some of these ideas back to their different communities.”</p><p>More than half a century later, the potential death knell came just after 4.30pm on Tuesday with <a href="https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/15/arts/music/kennedy-center-trump-name-inscription-judge-ruling.html">a perfunctory announcement</a> on the public address system: “The centre is now closed to the public. Please exit the centre by way of the Hall of States.” Soon barricades had been erected and security guards were blocking access.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/sep/19/trump-kennedy-center-future">Continue reading...</a></description>
